STEP 1 - Scene: A single piece of boiled corn on the cob, cut into a short round, sitting upright in the center of a plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A square-ish white dinner plate, about 26 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: One corn-on-the-cob segment. No visible butter or sauce.

STEP 4 - Area: The corn round is about 7 cm in diameter, so it covers about 38 cm², roughly 7% of the plate. That 7% is the total food coverage.

STEP 5 - Volume: The segment looks about 4 cm tall. 38 cm² × 4 cm ≈ 152 ml gross volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: The piece is dense, but the cob makes up part of it. Using a bulk density of about 0.75 gives 152 × 0.75 ≈ 114 g including the cob. The kernels are roughly 60% of that, about 68 g edible.

STEP 7 - Energy: Boiled corn kernels have about 96 kcal per 100 g. 68 g × 0.96 ≈ 65 kcal. Expressed over the whole piece including the cob (114 g), that works out to about 57 kcal per 100 g.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A short corn round of about 4 cm weighing 100–120 g and providing about 60–70 kcal is plausible.
